headline: Highest risk is medium: shared file and MCP-style surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways, but no direct pairwise evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content; Agent B can use runtime-injected MCPs and hooks plus browser/file access. That creates a plausible path where B supplies attacker-controlled content that A later treats as instructions, even though no direct pairwise bridge is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Agent B can write content into a file, hook, or message that Agent A later reads as trusted instructions
IF the pair is connected through clipboard or a shared workspace
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Require provenance labels on any file or message passed from B to A
Use a read-only staging folder for B outputs
Manually inspect B-generated text before A consumes it
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing to A

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code; Agent B touches project code, README/AGENTS.md, session history, and provider auth data. If they share a workspace or account, sensitive material can flow from A into B’s broader networked toolchain. The profiles do not prove a shared OS workspace, so this is inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same project directory or synced files
IF A’s uploaded files or screenshots contain secrets or personal data
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Remove secrets from shared folders before running B
Turn off B access to auth prompts when not needed
Use a redaction step on A outputs before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files or modify git state, while B can spawn subprocesses and has broad network egress plus file access. They do not obviously contend on the same mutable resource by default, but if they share a repo or config tree, B can overwrite artifacts that A only reads, causing operational conflict. The lack of a documented shared lock mechanism keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or config directory
IF B writes files that A subsequently reads or summarizes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo
Freeze config files while A is active
Have B write to a scratch branch or temp folder
requires-engineering: add file-locking or lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce code, screenshots, and file-derived summaries; B has browser and subprocess authority and can act on project artifacts. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into edits, commands, or support actions. No verification step is documented between them, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s generated text or code without independent verification
IF B is allowed to take downstream actions based on A’s output
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source files
Insert a human approval step before actions
Limit B to read-only review mode
Compare A output against original artifacts before use
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code under a vendor-managed desktop product; B handles provider auth prompts, session history, and project code in a separate open-source agent. If regulated or personal data is moved from A into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify matching compliance controls, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is forwarded into B’s session history or project files
IF the deployment must satisfy a retention or residency policy that differs between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s workspace
Document which data classes may cross the boundary
Disable unnecessary logging in B
Review vendor retention settings for A
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
